subject: mathematics
question_text: If a, b and c represent the vertices A, B and C respectively of triangle ABC, then prove that |(a×b) + (b×c) + (c×a)| is twice the area of triangle ABC.

mark_split.label: Write the two sides as vectors

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.105 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 161. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed SAQ on its length and shape. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: none — this answer carries no year tag. A general proof with no numbers. The cyclic sum on the left is not obviously an area — expanding (b−a)×(c−a) is what turns one into the other. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Write the two sides as vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. With a, b, c as position vectors, the two sides from A are AB = b − a and AC = c − a.
lines: The position vectors are OA = a, OB = b, OC = c.

recall.must_convey: That AB = b − a and AC = c − a.
accept: A B is b minus a and A C is c minus a
the sides from A are found by subtracting the position vector of A
write the two sides as vectors first
A B ante b minus a, A C ante c minus a
form the two sides from vertex A

steps.why: Both sides must start at the SAME vertex for the cross product to give that triangle's area. Starting one at A and one at B would give a different figure.
common_mistakes: Using a and b directly as the sides.

steps.label: Quote the area formula
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Area = ½|AB × AC|, so twice the area is |AB × AC| — which is what the question is really about.

recall.must_convey: That the area is ½|AB × AC|, so twice the area is |(b − a) × (c − a)|.
accept: the area is half the magnitude of the cross product so twice the area is that magnitude
two times the area equals mod of b minus a cross c minus a
quote the triangle area formula and double it
area half cross product, so twice area cross product magnitude
twice the area is the cross product magnitude

steps.why: The question asks for TWICE the area precisely because that removes the ½ and leaves a clean cross product — the statement is shaped to fit the formula.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the ½ in the area formula.
Proving the area rather than twice the area.

steps.label: Expand the cross product
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Expand as if multiplying brackets, but keep the ORDER — the cross product is not commutative. The a × a term is zero.

recall.must_convey: That expanding gives b×c − b×a − a×c + a×a, that a×a = 0, and that reversing the two negative terms gives the required cyclic sum.
accept: expand keeping the order, a cross a is zero, and reversing the two minus terms gives the cyclic sum
minus b cross a is a cross b and minus a cross c is c cross a
the cross product of a vector with itself is zero
a cross a zero, order marchi signs flip cheyyali
expand and rearrange to the required sum

steps.why: Reversing the order of a cross product flips its sign, so −b×a and a×b are the same thing. That single fact turns the expansion into the cyclic sum the question names.
common_mistakes: Treating the cross product as commutative and cancelling terms.
